title: Spirit in playing; finding the bass at high school
summary: If it is not spiritual don't play it; he discovered an aluminum bass in his junior year.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Well I had talked about Cannonball and Lester Young, and you were saying that their music was spiritual just in a different way.

Well if it ain’t spiritual don’t play it. If it’s not — you know your spirit is what makes you you know play the instrument. And it means if you’re not spiritual you’re ain’t feeling nothing so like Elvin Jones used to say, “If he ain’t playing nothing, get him off the stage and let somebody else get up there and play it.” So the various perceptions and concepts that all of these great musicians have brought to our ears are highly respected, it’s just that everybody’s doing it their own way. And for instance me, since this thing is about me, what was it — I at the conclusion of a band rehearsal at my high school my junior year I had put my clarinet into a little box and was now reaching across something on the floor that kind of prevented access to the compartment where I would store my clarinet. And I looked down and there was a bass. I said, “Oh, huh.” So I put the clarinet in and I picked the bass up and played a note and I said, right away it was like whoa, that sounds wonderful. Right? So I tried to play the thing. It was an old — the bass was like made of metal.
